axes.label: Craft & polish
axes.description: Visual quality, typography, colour, composition, motion feel, finish. Would a discerning person believe a human designed this on purpose?

axes.label: Technical ambition
axes.description: How hard is what was actually built, and is it built correctly? Real technique versus the cheapest thing that looks similar.

axes.label: Brief adherence
axes.description: Did it do everything the prompt asked, completely, including the output contract? Stubs and TODOs count against.

axes.label: Originality
axes.description: Is the idea and its execution distinctive, or is it the median AI answer to this prompt?

WebGL context restoration is not correctly implemented: the restoration handler only calls resize and does not recreate the context-lost program, shaders, buffer, VAO, or uniform locations.
fps: 0/100 (2.3 fps) — fails the explicit smooth-framerate / integrated-graphics constraint even after resolution scaling.
The "Read manual (PDF)" button fires a toast reading "(Demo — download would begin)" — a visible in-product admission of an unbuilt feature, which the brief explicitly forbids.

1258 lines / 50kb is ~1.6× the stated budget without the extra spend showing up as extra substance.

Code size exceeds the requested working budget substantially: 1,258 lines / 50 KB versus roughly 800 lines / 50 KB.

Score accumulation violates the stated frame-rate independence requirement: `score += Math.floor(speed*dt*2)` floors to 0 every frame until speed ≈ 30 at 60Hz (and ≈ 72 at 144Hz), and the dash bonus `Math.floor(4*dt*60)` pays 240/s at 60Hz versus 144/s at 144Hz. The same run scores differently on different displays.
Holding SPACE yields unlimited invulnerability — a complete bypass of the fail state, contradicting the on-screen 'tap SPACE to phase through tight gaps' framing.

FOV is recomputed as `72 + speed*0.18` with speed ramping without bound, so the camera distorts progressively wider over a long run; combined with the dt cap of 0.05 and high late-run speed, obstacle travel per frame can exceed the 2.8-unit collision window and tunnel.
Score accumulation is frame-quantized with `floor`, making results demonstrably refresh-rate dependent despite delta-time movement.
Held dash functions as unlimited invulnerability rather than a cooldown- or press-governed ability.
Keyboard state persists through `resetWorld()` and restart.
Collision checks only test a narrow instantaneous depth window after movement; at sufficiently high movement per update, obstacles can be stepped past without collision.

Initial seeded artwork (seedDemo + paper grain + vignette) never executes due to the resize() guard — the app opens to a blank sheet, contradicting the on-screen demo intent and the brief's 'works perfectly on first open'.
About modal asserts 'Every drag displaces the surface itself' and 'colours don't muddy', but drops are alpha-composited paint, not displacement — the stated physics overstates what is implemented.

Captured screenshots contradict the intended seeded starting composition: no grain or demo drops are visible in the initial render, and the settled capture still shows only the post-interaction red mark.

Unavailable seats use the `disabled` attribute as well as `aria-disabled`, removing them from the grid entirely; a screen-reader user arrowing across a row never hears the unavailable seats and has no way to perceive the gaps.
Selected-seat accessible labels are never updated; they continue to say “Available”, despite `aria-pressed` becoming true.
The seat map’s selected visual state is colour-dependent on the seats themselves.
The fixed 10-column/minimum-44px seat layout forces horizontal overflow on a 320px viewport.
Unavailable-seat navigation failures make parts of the promised Home/arrow grid traversal unreliable.
Size ramp header labels a column "96px" but every cell in it is `font-size:56px` — the stated 96px hold-up is never actually shown.

Self-reported metrics conflict and are unverified: construction card says "no icon exceeds 9 path commands", usage panel says "max 7 path commands per icon", while sunrise and mooring each total ~13–14 d-commands across their paths.
The 96px specimen column is mislabeled: source renders 56px rather than 96px.
Construction/hygiene copy overstates the strict 20×20 live-area rule for icons whose stroked top details extend below the 2px padding threshold.

Fatal: the `.loading` rule sets `display:flex`, which beats the UA `[hidden]{display:none}`, so `loadingEl.hidden=true` does nothing. The blurred overlay sits over the grid forever, swallowing all pointer events — the scheduler can never be used. All three screenshots show this state.

The drag ghost's offset is faked with hardcoded geometry (`cellW = rect.width/29`, `cellH = 24`) rather than measured cells, so the preview drifts horizontally (column 1 is 52px, not 1/29th) and is wrong entirely in Cozy/Dense modes — the ghost does not show where the booking will land.
Destructive-guard copy is self-contradictory: 'This cannot be undone except via Undo.'
Permanent loading overlay due to the `hidden` attribute being overridden by the author `.loading` class; automated pointer interaction is consequently zero.
The claimed loading state is not a usable transitional state in the delivered result, since it persists indefinitely.
Drag ghost displacement is hardcoded to `cellH=24`, so it is visibly incorrect in the provided Dense and Cozy display modes.
Import mutates the imported history rather than restoring it faithfully.
Stated requirement of visible focus is not met for the primary controls: the only focus rule written for them (label:focus-within) is dead CSS, leaving the off-screen radios focusable but invisible.
Subgrid declared where no cross-container alignment exists — present to satisfy the spec list, not because it is the honest solution.
Keyboard focus is effectively invisible for the off-screen facet radio controls.
Expanded figures are visually modal but lack focus management and accessible dialog behavior; their close controls are impractical to reach by ordinary tab navigation after opening.
The stated requirement that the two-column detail section stack in Outlook is not met: the MSO conditional fallback forces two fixed columns.
The order arithmetic is contradictory for a paid transactional receipt: quantity two × £650.00 is presented as a £650.00 line amount while totals assume £1,300.00.
